analysis:
Examined MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift: the base_text unit (lines 1018-1552) and the head_text unit (lines 1-529). The patch excerpt is truncated and the head text stops at line 529, so most changed head ranges are not visible: 743, 865, 1195, 1366-1393, 1431-1434, 1468-1491. Changed behavior I could see only through the patch excerpt: (1) modelType is now passed into the reasoning-prompt probe at two sites; (2) the router is constructed with `streamedCalls: prepared`, and a new `router.streamsToolCalls` branch calls `router.finishToolCalls(truncated: stopReason == "length")` to emit streamed tool-call deltas, then re-validates the set. This is parser and streaming behavior inside the provider process after the E2E decrypt boundary. It does not touch the encryption or sealing path (T-008), attestation, authorization (TB-011/T-053), or prefix-cache scoping (T-041); cacheScope handling is unchanged.

The base text shows the existing fail-closed pattern: `releaseBox.fire()` and `cancelUpstream` run on every error exit, and the native media terminal drain is preserved. I could not confirm the new streaming branch keeps that pattern. Open questions for integration: whether the `streamsToolCalls` path (a) fires `releaseBox` on every throw and cancellation exit, to avoid leaking the model reservation (T-010 and T-029 availability); (b) still enforces ToolConstraintValidation for required or named tool modes before the first delta is emitted, since `auto` calls are validated per frame; (c) emits no plaintext outside the existing sealed response path; and (d) handles a `length`-truncated call safely. The router implementation (NativeToolStreamRouter) and the tail of the truncated patch were not supplied, so no finding can be supported from the visible evidence.
